title: The Woman Who Imagined Computers
paragraphs: Ada Lovelace was born in 1815. Her father was the famous poet Lord Byron. Ada studied mathematics and science, and her mother encouraged this.

As a young woman, she met Charles Babbage, an inventor and mathematician. Babbage planned a large machine called the Analytical Engine. It was designed to follow instructions and do many kinds of calculations. Ada wrote long notes about this machine. In them, she explained step by step how it could work out a series of special numbers. Many people call this the first computer program.

Ada also had an idea that was far ahead of her time. She believed that such a machine might one day work with music and other symbols, not only with numbers. Sadly, the machine was never finished, and Ada died young. Today, people see her as an early pioneer of computing.
